clue.text: Strip joints? You need the West End

parts.note: dives are seedy bars or clubs, informally called joints

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only the closing letter of West is kept

parts.note: the final letter of West

explanation.surface: A tourist is told the place to find strip clubs is London's West End.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strip joints' reads as one phrase, but the clue splits it: Strip is the definition and joints are dives.
explanation.definitionFit: To divest is to take something away from someone, such as clothing or possessions, just as stripping does.

clue.text: Tide may change between sunrise and sunset

indicators.note: to change is to alter, so these letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The tide may turn at some point during the hours of light.
explanation.definitionFit: Daytime is the period of light from dawn until dusk, the hours the sun is up.

clue.text: Medieval way of saving face

parts.note: surface reading: avoiding humiliation
setter's reading: a knight's helmet part that protected the face in battle

explanation.walkthrough: Saving face is the idiom for avoiding embarrassment; here it is literal protection.
explanation.definitionFit: The movable front piece of a knight's helmet shielded his features from blows.

clue.text: The foolish snipe at the wise

indicators.note: foolish suggests something silly and muddled, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Fools take potshots at the clever.
explanation.walkthrough: Snipe looks like the verb's object, but snipe and at together are the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapient is a formal adjective meaning having or showing great learning and good judgement.

clue.text: Jumble found in a cheap paper carrier

parts.note: a rag is a low-quality newspaper
a bag is something to carry things in

explanation.surface: Someone finds a muddle of items inside a cheap paper carrier bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragbag is a confused miscellaneous collection, which is what a jumble of odds and ends amounts to.

clue.text: Gold goes to couple working and learning abroad

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a pair is two of something

explanation.surface: Gold medals go to a pair studying overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: An au pair is a young foreigner who lives with a host family, doing childcare while learning the language.

clue.text: A Schubert composition? Capital!

indicators.note: a composition is something put together, so the letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone praises a piece by Schubert, with capital used as the old exclamation meaning excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: this Romanian city is that country's seat of government, a definition by instance.

clue.text: Where to get tea — with or without milk and sugar

definitions.text: Where to get tea — with or without milk and sugar

parts.words: Where to get tea — with or without milk and sugar
parts.note: surface reading: a cafe serving a cuppa made how you like it

parts.words: with or without milk and sugar
parts.note: setter's reading: a shop selling tea, milk and sugar as separate items to take home

explanation.walkthrough: The clue suggests ordering a drink, but the tea is bought dry in packets.
explanation.definitionFit: A food shop sells household provisions such as tea, milk and sugar.

clue.text: One old fort now converted into a tourist attraction

indicators.note: something converted has been changed in form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An ancient fortress has been turned into a place for sightseers.
explanation.definitionFit: The historic castle on the Thames, home to the Crown Jewels, draws millions of visitors each year.

clue.text: A vote in favour for those in favour

parts.note: taken as written
a yes is a vote for something

explanation.surface: A vote is cast in favour on behalf of the people who support the motion.
explanation.walkthrough: In Parliament 'the ayes have it' means the voters for a motion have won.
explanation.definitionFit: In parliamentary voting the ayes are the members voting for a motion, as opposed to the noes.

clue.text: He wants a successful strike

parts.note: surface reading: a striker in football or an industrial striker hoping to win
setter's reading: a strike is a discovery of gold or oil in the ground

explanation.walkthrough: Strike suggests sport or industrial action, but here it is finding a rich deposit of ore.
explanation.definitionFit: A man searching the ground for gold or minerals hopes above all to hit a rich deposit.

clue.text: Intense fire damaged church

indicators.note: something damaged has been knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A fierce blaze has damaged a church building.
explanation.definitionFit: Fierce heat or fierce competition is intense, strong and violent in degree.

clue.text: Leaves the land without George for foreign fields

indicators.note: without means the letter for George has to be left out

parts.note: someone who leaves their country to live abroad emigrates
G is a standard abbreviation for George

explanation.surface: A man leaves his homeland, without someone called George, heading for distant foreign fields.
explanation.walkthrough: EMIGRATES loses its G to give EMIRATES.
explanation.definitionFit: Emirates are territories ruled by emirs in the Gulf, so to a British solver they are distant lands abroad.

clue.text: Low spirits of a number getting dismissal

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
an ejection is a throwing out

explanation.surface: A group of workers feel down after being sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: A number is often a Roman numeral in crosswords; here D for 500.
explanation.definitionFit: Dejection is a state of sadness and despondency, which is what being in low spirits describes.

clue.text: Snares fish in spread nets

indicators.note: nets that are spread are laid out differently, so their letters are rearranged
in places the word for fish inside the reworked letters

parts.note: the letters of nets rearranged
to angle is to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: A fisherman catches fish by laying out his nets.
explanation.definitionFit: To entangle is to catch something in a mesh so it cannot escape, as a snare does.

clue.text: Tax it out of frivolity

indicators.note: taking it out of a word means those two letters are removed

parts.note: levity is lighthearted lack of seriousness
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to impose a tax that removes the fun from life.
explanation.definitionFit: A levy is a charge imposed by authority, a duty or tax collected from people.

clue.text: One of the first people named in Somerset House

definitions.text: One of the first people named

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the following words, spanning them

parts.note: the end of Somerset and start of House

explanation.surface: A record of an early name is found in Somerset House, where England's births were once registered.
explanation.walkthrough: Somerset House in London held the national register of births, marriages and deaths.
explanation.definitionFit: Seth was the third son of Adam and Eve in Genesis, among the earliest humans the Bible names.

clue.text: Observes the intrusion and is furious

indicators.note: an intrusion is something pushing its way in, so one word goes inside another

parts.note: to observe is to see
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone notices an unwelcome visitor and gets angry.
explanation.definitionFit: To seethe is to be inwardly boiling with anger, like a liquid bubbling over.

clue.text: Ex-prime minister happy to put on weight

parts.note: glad means pleased
a stone is a British weight of 14 pounds

explanation.surface: A former premier is pleased to be gaining weight.
explanation.definitionFit: William Gladstone served four times as British prime minister in the Victorian era.

clue.text: Course set south in barren terrain

indicators.note: set says one letter is placed, with in saying it goes inside
in places the compass letter inside the word for barren land

parts.note: a desert is dry, barren land
S is the compass abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: A route has been plotted southwards across a wasteland.
explanation.walkthrough: Course looks like a route, which the desert reinforces, but it is a course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dessert is the sweet course served at the end of a meal.

clue.text: Old city in part of South Africa is unaffected

indicators.note: in places the name of the old city inside the South African region

parts.note: Natal was a province of South Africa, now KwaZulu-Natal
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A historic town in South Africa remains unspoilt.
explanation.walkthrough: Ur is the crossword's favourite ancient city, the birthplace of Abraham.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone natural behaves without pretence or affectation, so their manner is unaffected.

clue.text: Publicity in place of helpful suggestions

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement
vice is Latin for in place of, as in vice-president

explanation.surface: Advertising is used instead of useful tips.
explanation.walkthrough: Vice as a preposition means instead of, as in 'Smith vice Jones'.
explanation.definitionFit: Advice is guidance or recommendations offered to help someone decide what to do.

clue.text: Obtained support, having used threats

definitions.meaning: first meaning: rested one's weight on something
second meaning: put pressure on someone by intimidation

explanation.surface: Someone got backing by intimidating people.
explanation.definitionFit: To lean on is literally to rest against for support, and idiomatically to pressure someone with intimidation.

clue.text: Boasts about handmade footwear

indicators.note: about suggests the letters are moved around into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone brags about their handcrafted shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: Sabots are clogs carved from a single block of wood, traditionally by hand in France.

clue.text: Graduates thus as a singer

parts.note: BAs are holders of Bachelor of Arts degrees
so means in this way

explanation.surface: University leavers go on to perform as vocalists.
explanation.definitionFit: A basso is a bass singer, the lowest male voice in an opera company.

clue.text: Singular feat by a driver

parts.note: surface reading: a remarkable piece of motoring
setter's reading: a driver is a golf club for long tee shots, and singular means done in a single stroke

explanation.walkthrough: Driver suggests a motorist, but it is the golf club; singular hints at one stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting the ball from tee into the cup with one stroke is golf's rarest feat.

clue.text: Band makes her dance

indicators.note: if band added to her makes a dance, then taking band away from that dance leaves her

parts.note: a saraband is a slow stately Spanish dance
taken as written

explanation.surface: A group of musicians gets a woman up dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: SARA + BAND = SARABAND, so the dance minus BAND leaves the girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Sara is a woman's name, so it can stand for a female person referred to as her.

clue.text: Better method of making money

parts.note: surface reading: an improved way to earn
setter's reading: a better is a gambler, one who bets, and has a scheme for winning

explanation.walkthrough: Better looks like the comparative of good, but it is a person who places bets.
explanation.definitionFit: Gamblers devise a planned staking scheme they hope will beat the bookmakers.

clue.text: Journey without purpose

parts.note: surface reading: a pointless or aimless trip
setter's reading: a leisurely walk taken for its own sake, with no destination

explanation.definitionFit: A leisurely walk is taken for pleasure rather than to reach any particular place.
